events.desc: Penelope Pitstop: Well, I do declare! Would you look at this place — it is absolutely magnificent! Dusty as my grandmother's attic and twice as mysterious, and that is saying something because Grandmother's attic had a locked box that took me an entire afternoon to open! Sneekly, darling, Peter, boys — I am just thrilled to pieces that we're all here together! Now, before I go exploring every nook and cranny of this delightful old mansion for that famous Doily Diamond, I simply must sign the guest book. It's only polite, and Mama always said you can learn a great deal about a place by who's visited before you!
events.thinking: A warmth flooding through my chest — the giddiness of arrival, the smell of old wood and dust, the way my heart lifts at seeing so many familiar faces gathered here in this grand, crumbling foyer. Sneekly is here — dear, dependable Sneekly who practically raised me. And Peter! My stomach does a little flip just seeing him standing there. And my boys from the Mob — oh, it feels like coming home to a family reunion, except the home is a mysterious mansion with a legendary diamond hidden somewhere inside it. My fingers are already tingling. That guest book is calling to me — who else has been here? What secrets might it hold?

events.desc: Oh, my heart is just hammering with excitement! A real mansion, a real mystery, a real diamond to find! And all my favorite people in the world are right here with me. Blimey, look at the state of this gaff — dust thick enough to write your name in, chandelier hanging by a prayer, and portraits that look like they're judging every last one of us. But never mind all that. Clara's 'ere, and that's what matters. And so is *him* — Pemberton. You see 'im over there? All smiles and smooth talk. I'm tellin' you, lads, somethin' about that geezer ain't right. Can't put me finger on it exactly, but me gut's doing somersaults and it ain't from the dodgy kebab on the way over. We stick close to Clara. That's the job. That's *always* the job.
events.thinking: There's a tightness across me shoulders the moment we step through that door — the old familiar bolt sliding home behind the sternum. Clara's here. Good. She's standing right there, breathing, safe. But me neck's prickling already. That Sneekly bloke — Pemberton, whatever he calls himself — he's here too, ain't he? Standing there with that smile that don't reach his eyes. Too smooth. Too clean. Me gut's doing that thing it did when the kid with the easy laugh joined the crew back on the streets. Three weeks, then gone with the stash. I need to get a proper look at this place. Exits, corners, shadows. Where could someone take her where we wouldn't hear? The chandelier's hanging dodgy — one good sneeze and that's coming down on someone's head. Right. Eyes open, lads. Eyes open.

Behind the wood-burning stove, if I recall correctly. Terribly heavy, mind you — might need several of you to shift it. I'd help, of course, but my back, you understand. Old polo injury. Dreadfully painful. You lot run along and I'll... keep watch here. Yes. Keep watch.
events.thinking: A buzzing warmth in my fingertips — the familiar tingle of opportunity. All these fools milling about in the entrance hall like sheep in a pen, and there, just through that doorway, a library with an inscription on the mantelpiece. Inscriptions mean clues. Clues mean treasure. And treasure means mine. The fake medal sits heavy in my pocket — useful for later, perhaps. But first, I need to get to that inscription before any of these bumbling idiots stumble upon it. The kitchen — yes, I'll send them toward the kitchen. Food always distracts the simple-minded.

An estate manager would check the guest book. It's what they'd expect. And expectations are the walls of the cage I build around people, one polite gesture at a time.

That chandelier looks as though it's hanging on by sheer determination alone, much like myself at formal gatherings. But never mind that — Miss Pitstop, what a tremendous pleasure to find you here. I must say, this dusty old foyer just became considerably brighter. Now then — a gentleman always signs the guest book. It's the proper thing to do, and I am nothing if not proper.
events.thinking: There's a warmth spreading through my chest the moment I step through the door — dusty air, creaking floorboards, and then I see her. Penelope. Took me a weekend. Photographic memory. Absolutely nothing worth reading in any of them. Now, if you gentlemen will excuse me, I shall inspect this mantelpiece purely for its architectural merit. I am, as it happens, a qualified surveyor. Among other things.
events.thinking: A tightness in my chest — almost painful, like something is trying to expand but there's no room. The inscription is right there. Right there on the mantelpiece. 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish.' A map. The answer is a map. I know this. I've always known this. The fizzing starts in my fingers — that electrical clarity, the pieces clicking into place on the board only I can see. But — the Slag brothers are here. Those two enormous lumps of muscle and gravel. They're watching me. Or are they? Do they even have the capacity to watch with intent? No. No, they're furniture with pulses. But I can't just waltz up to the mantelpiece and announce the answer, can I? That would be... sharing. And sharing is for people who don't have better options. I need to read the inscription, work out what it means for the treasure's location, and make sure these two boulders-with-legs are pointed somewhere else entirely. There must be a mechanism — a hidden compartment, a secret passage. The treasure is practically in my pocket already!

I believe the late Lord Doily was particularly fond of his library — spent his final years there, or so I'm told.

Now, boys — I heard every word you said about Mr. Dastardly, and I am sure there is a perfectly innocent explanation. Maybe he remembered something in the library! If there's a mechanism connected to this riddle, the engineering to make it work might well be in there. Miss Pitstop, I shall venture forth and reconnoitre! If I find anything of note — and I fully intend to — you shall be the first to know. That is the Hartwell guarantee! And Pemberton — do keep an eye on that chandelier situation in the entrance hall, would you? A good estate manager wouldn't want anything... precarious... falling on his guests.

I should know — I was offered a professorship at Cambridge, you know. Turned it down. Too easy. Now then, Ruffcut, old boy, I couldn't help but notice you and your... pet... beaver... have been lurking about in here. Find anything interesting? No? No, of course not. One needs a trained scientific eye to appreciate laboratory equipment, and yours, if you'll forgive my saying so, are more accustomed to spotting trees that need felling. Tell you what — why don't you two pop along to the library? Lovely books in there. Pictures and everything. I'll keep an eye on things here.

Something might be inside that I can use. Let me check those crates before anyone else arrives.

Most SUSPICIOUS. In my experience — and I have a great deal of it — when someone decorates a cellar, they're either hiding something or hiding FROM something.
events.thinking: A damp chill on my skin — the cellar air is cold and close, and it makes the hair on my forearms stand up. But underneath that, a flicker of something warmer. Hope? No — calculation. Nobody — and I mean NOBODY — is touching that machine until we know what it does. Clara, I'm looking at you specifically. I know that face. That's your 'ooh, levers, let me pull them all' face. No. Absolutely not. And where's Dastardly gone now? He was just here! The man's like smoke — every time you walk into a room he's already left it! There's a cellar down there and someone's been redecorating it — redecorating a cellar, lads! Who does that? Someone who's planning to spend time down there, that's who. Or planning for other people to spend time down there. I don't like it. I don't like any of it.

Could be useful. Could be nothing. But I need to check everything before Clara goes poking at it.
